description: Antony served as Caesar's officer in Gaul (54-50 BCE) and at Pharsalus (48 BCE); Caesar appointed him Magister Equitum and co-consul for 44 BCE.
note: Antony was also distantly related to Caesar through his mother Julia Antonia, who was a cousin of Caesar.

description: Antony and Octavian were political rivals after Caesar's death, temporary allies in the Second Triumvirate (43-33 BCE), then open enemies leading to the War of Actium (32-30 BCE).
note: Relationship evolved: initial hostility (44-43 BCE) → triumviral alliance (43-33 BCE) → final war (32-30 BCE).

description: Antony entered a personal and political alliance with Cleopatra VII from 41 BCE until their joint deaths in 30 BCE. They had three children together: Alexander Helios, Cleopatra Selene II, and Ptolemy Philadelphus.
note: Antony recognized Caesarion (Cleopatra's son with Julius Caesar) as Caesar's legitimate heir in the Donations of Alexandria, challenging Octavian's position.

description: Lepidus was Antony's fellow triumvir (43-36 BCE). Lepidus was stripped of his powers by Octavian in 36 BCE after attempting to seize Sicily; Antony did not intervene.
Antony married Octavia, sister of Octavian, in 40 BCE as a political union sealing the Pact of Brundisium. He divorced her in 32 BCE. They had two daughters.
note: Plutarch portrays Octavia as a virtuous Roman wife abandoned by Antony for Cleopatra, part of the pro-Augustan narrative.

description: Fulvia was Antony's third wife, married c. 47-46 BCE. She actively managed Antony's political interests in Italy and, with Lucius Antonius, led the Perusine War against Octavian (41-40 BCE).
note: Fulvia died in 40 BCE at Sicyon, Greece, which facilitated Antony's reconciliation with Octavian.

description: Cicero delivered fourteen Philippics against Antony (44-43 BCE), denouncing him as a tyrant and threat to the Republic. Antony had Cicero proscribed and killed in December 43 BCE.
note: According to Plutarch, Antony had Cicero's head and hands displayed on the Rostra in the Forum.

description: Brutus was one of Caesar's assassins. Antony defeated Brutus at the first Battle of Philippi (42 BCE); Brutus took his own life after the second engagement.
Cassius was a leading conspirator in Caesar's assassination. Antony's forces defeated Cassius at Philippi in 42 BCE; Cassius committed suicide after the first battle.
Agrippa was Octavian's chief admiral and general. Agrippa defeated Antony's fleet at Actium (31 BCE) and commanded the forces that took Alexandria (30 BCE).
Lucius Antonius was Antony's younger brother. As consul in 41 BCE, Lucius and Fulvia led the Perusine War against Octavian. He was spared after defeat at Perusia.

Antony recognized Caesarion, Cleopatra's son with Julius Caesar, as Caesar's legitimate heir and co-ruler in the Donations of Alexandria (34 BCE). Octavian had Caesarion killed after Alexandria fell in 30 BCE.

Decimus Brutus was a former Caesarian who joined the assassination conspiracy. Antony besieged him at Mutina in 43 BCE; the siege was broken by Octavian and the consuls. Decimus was later killed while fleeing.
